titleStmt.title: A volume of rhapsodical meditations and visions (Rawl. D. 1262)
titleStmt.author: Ann Bathurst

div1.p:
The God of Abraham, the Fear of Isaac, & The Authors Inducements the Strength of Israël; even The God & Father of our Lord & Saviour Jesus Christ taught me whilst I was yet young: He taught me to goe, leading me by the armes Hos. 11. 3. in footsteps that I knew not, yet understood I not that it was He yt led me; but afterwards when more of age I perceived He taught me step by step, how I should walk in a Child-like Obedience to His Divine Attributes, with large Leadings in His Mercifull Love- Nature-Love, giving me great experiences of His Mercifull Love, and greatly to acquiesce in all his wise Dispensations; thus teaching me that His wisom knew what was best, and that His Fatherly Love was so great as all should work together for good to Them that love Him, and are called thereunto. And though His teachings & Conduct I for many years concealed, and so intended still; yet since recollecting what use it might be off for my self and others,^ I was much press'd --- in Spirit to^ to write Them down,------ as also afterwards ^ by some ffriends so to doe, for the better solicited reception of what further Manifestations The Lord now in these later dayes has made declared unto me (not for my self only but others also.) Therefor I'm not willing to hide it in a napkin, well knowing that the same spirit wch led me is but one Spirit, and will teach all that do but adhere thereunto; for God is the same yesterday, to day & for ever: who at sundry times Heb. 1. 1, 2. and in divers manners spake in time past unto the ffathers by the Prophets, hath now in these last days spoke to us by His Son, whom He hath made Heir of all things; putting all things under Him, spoiling all Principalities & Powers. For in that He put all Heb. 2, 8. in Subjection under Him, He left nothing that is not put under Him: but now we see not yet all things put under Him; but we see Jesus crowned with Glory & honour, yt at the Name of Jesus the Saviour, that saveth his People from their Sins, every knee^, all Homage, glory & honour, & Obedience ofPhil. 2. 10,11. Things in Heaven, & things in Earth, & things under ye Earth^ should bend should be given: and yt every Tongue should confess that Jesus is Lord to ye glory of God the Father, to whom be glo-
ry & honour, dominion & praise now, henceforth & eternally.

I was taught as I've said when I was young. The boughs when young & tender will yeild easily, so it is with ye tender soul before it grows old in sin. And surely as the first fruits & firstlings of the fflock God required should be offer'd & sacrificed to Him, so is the first of our age: wch, as it is the most acceptable to God, so it is the most easy to Man; not having then such loads of guilt, if The Accuser should attempt to awaken.

It is I say much easier, yet not altogether easy: for about the Tenth year of my age, I found the Accuser awaken in me a sence of sin, yet not of any one particular Sin, for I could remember none, but as if all my life had been a continued act of Sin: wch caused in me such great horrour & anguish, of as even to despair of mercy; or at least to question whither I could expect mercy: but I was soon stayed with David's praising God in the 30th psalm (hearing a sermon ps. 30. 1,2,3. on it) I will extoll Thee O Lord! for Thou hast lifted me up and hast not made my foes to rejoyce over me: &c. So yt my sorrow ecchoed my joy. And in another sermon I learned watchfullness at all tymes, lest Sathan should gett advantage over me, even to watch the use of things lawfull, & against all or any appearance of evil. All which I still acknowledge I owe first to God, & secondarily much was suck'd in from pious Parents & Religious education, whereby both by precept & example I was accustomed to pray.

And about the fifteenth year of my age for my encouragement to pray thereunto, I obtain'd a promise in Prayer, yt the same should be answered; declaring to me how, & by what sign I should know yt That prayer was answered. Wch was decordingly fulfilled at its appointed season. And having had such experience how God heard, & in hearing answered, it did for the future encourage me in all the pressures of my soul, to pour out my requests unto Him, who has required ps. 50. 15. yt we should Call upon Him in the day of trouble, and hath also promised He will deliver us; and then we must glorifie Him. and we do best glorifie Him by believing unto Obedience.

About the Eighteenth year of my age; seeing the strict practice of some about me, it awakned in me a serious search how it was with my soul, to what end I was born, and to what end I ought to live? and finding little to accuse my self off, as to sins of Commission, I enquired into sins of Ommission; Dan. 6. 10,13. and in Scripture record I found yt Daniel prayed three ps. 119. 164. times a day, and David said, seven times a day do I praise
Thee: (wch certain number may signifie many times, yet do I think yt David prayed seven sett times a day: for so He seems to insinuate, when he says, a.Evening, & morning, & at noon will a. ps. 55. 17.I pray. b.I prevent the night watches. c.at midnight I will arise b. ps. 119. 148. to give thanks unto Thee. I prevents the dawning of ye morningc. v. 62. & cried. &c.) and in 1. Thess. 5. 16. It is said; Rejoyce ever more, pray without ceasing, &c. but I thought it only referred to sett times; wch accordingly with all privacy I began: but my mouth was stopt like one struck dumb; wch caused great consternation & terrour, saying within my self; have I so many sins, and can I beg pardon for none? and so many graces do I stand in need off, and is there not any one Grace I can ask for? yet still did I remain as one stupified and dumb, but filled with an awaked horrour & grief even to high despair: wch soon was still'd with this Inward reflection, I was Nothing, & could do nothing, not think in my heart oftof God without Divine assistance: and His assistance makes our acceptance.

Several disturbing Objections arose, but still I was answered to study duly rather than reward; teaching me yt thô I could not read his secret-will, yet I could read his revealed will, wch requires yt I should serve Him^(^at this time I had taken in The doctrine of Election, of wch I was afterward undeceived.): and so in his strength I resolved to throw my self upon Him, in the simple sincere, Child-like Obedience, that if I perished it should be in so doing: wch reminded me of the Men that went into the2. K. 7. 4. Camp of the Assyrians, who said, if we sitt at the gate see nothing but death attend us; and if the Assyrians save us alive we shall live; and if They kill us we shall but die. This then was my case, and these words instructed me; and good was That God like an anchor of hope to help & draw me thus to Him! I continued praying, hearing & reading; but often was the return of sorrows lest I should labour in vain: and little was applied to me from a Sermon or reading but reproof through the awakned sense of sin; as if it were spoken to none but me, putting far off all comfort.

And in some few moneths I was seized with sickness, and that somewhat dangerous; as for my own part, being before a stranger to sickness I did not question but I should die; wch caused me to mourn & weep to them that were with me telling them, I had no assurance of a better Life, now that I fear'd I was to die, having lived a long time in sin (being now about eighteen years & an half old.) Then some of them said to me, yt I had been well educated & brought up in all sobriety; not knowing, nor having so much as heard of the vanities that most then walked in. I answered, 'tis true I had
been well instructed, & did practise what I was capable off: when I was a Child I loved to pray with my sister, & to hear her pray. I lik'd to read The Bible & good Books, as for other books I^ since wch time I've hardly read any thing save the Bible thought them not worth my time & pains^ and I further said, yt I knew not of any one sin I lived in, wch was some stay, but it soon went off: and I said, all this is nothing; I did but like †a Child little understanding what I did. † A few days afterwards, all my sins were laid before me (as they were also some years agoe, as I have already said.) yet not one particular sin remembred, but yt all my whole life was like one act of sin, and that Hell was to receive me: I said I had deserved the hottest place of it: and I saw Hell open to me, a great black, dark pit; and I at the brink ready to go in: I acknowledg'd to the Lord He was very just if He did cast me in; and also yt He was very mercifull in keeping me out so long in the Land of the Living. I concluded & said yt now Hell was my portion, and God was to be praised for his long forbearance to the Children of Men; for He had been a just God if He had cast me into Hell and soon as I was born, for I had been conceived in sin & brought forth in inquity.

And as the Lord taught me He was just & mercifull, so He made me to consider his power, whither He was not able to save me out of this horrible Pit, thô I had deserved it. I did verily believe God was able to save me, though I was at the very brink of Hell just a going in; but whither God was willing to save me, This I feared; and thus continued a day or two: Then it was answered, if He was not as willing as well as able, none could have been saved; for it is only of ffree Grace yt we are saved, and how dost thou know but yt God will save Thee? I said, what, me? Yes, Thee. I said, I have nothing yt is good in me, a poor sinfull Creature: what is there in me yt God should pardon me? Then I was answered, 'Tis true nothing is in Thee, but (The Lord spake wth power) I will have mercy because I will have mercy, & because mercy pleaseth me; and I have pardoned thy sins freely, and will remember them no more. Most gladly did I receive this word, It putt more joy & gladness in my heart, than They have when ps. 4. 7.their corn & oyl & wine encreased. † And as before I saw Hell† open'd for me, so now I saw the Heavens open and an Angel in the Heavens ready to receive me. I had some questioning of this, how I could expect such mercy as this, being not worthy; I was answered, if God stayed to shew mercy till we were worthy to receive, we should never have mercy. Some other Objections arose to the like purpose, but all were answered; and so answered as never to question his Love, nor could The Tempter ever sett footing to disturb my peace & comfort ever since: but once
when Sin wrestled in me (as Esau & Jacob) I look up Rebekkahs speech & said, if it be so, why am I thus? if the Lord hath pardon'd me & graciously accepted me, why then doth sin still strive to overcome me? to make me speak unadviseably thô not sinfully? Then I lookt back & call'd to mind, how God came in by a mighty hand & a strong arm, and pulled me out of the claws of Sathan, & brought me from the Gates of Hell. And then considering how the Lord spake peace & silenced all my doubtings, and how He freely accepted me, and also the raptures of joy I then had; these & such like remembred made my spirit say, it is so, thôugh I am thus. Then how willing was I, yea I even longed to be with Christ, wch is best of all: to see That Christ wch I had now but a taste off, to see Him face to face; but had some desire after this, to live to glorify God; yt I might shew forth His praise that had done so much for me; but The Lord told me, He was all-Glorious in himself & needed not any Creature to sett forth his Glory. Then I thought what was I? God had many in the world He could make use off to sett forth his Glory, to declare it to the world, though I were might be call'd out of it. And I said, The Lord hath carried me on from strength to strength, and as He hath begun a good work, and hath gone on, so He will perfect it to the day of Redemption: He is the same yesterday, to day, & the same for ever.

I further said, now Lord, what wait I for! my expectation is from Thee; my soul longeth for Thee, for the Living God; when shall I come & appear before God? O the dread of wicked men! They call for mountains to fall on them, and the Hills to cover them, but O the sight of God is the Heaven of Heavens! ThoseWe that wait for & expect such things as these, what manner of men & women ought we to be in all holy conversation & godliness? How exact in our words, laying a watch on our lips & putting a bridle to our tongues, yt we sin not wth our mouths? How should we, as Christ did, go about doing good; and when God hath converted us,--strenthen our Brethren? We should communicate of our experience to others, we should not want grace by this, but we should encrease our graces: we should be in no Company without leaving some savour of good there, striving to season it. Oh the sins of Omission! how hard is it not to be guilty of omitting duties, that are required of every Man in their several stations & Conditions? besides the duties we omitt between God & the Soul, whereas it is our duty to pray; nay it is our priviledge & happiness yt God will hear & accept our prayers, yt He should let us converse & meditate on Him, and permitt us to fetch a Turn in Heaven, and that every day, yt we may be in Heaven by Meditation, as it were before our time, and receive the first ffruits of our spiritual Canaan in this Life. In keeping God's
Commandments ther's great reward even in this Life, as well as Eternal Happiness & enjoyment of God for ever hereafter: nay the Comfort a Child of God enjoys in this Life in God will make ammends for any afflictions He undergoes for Godbesides yt He will also give them Eternal mercies for every where there shall be no end, but They shall praise God to the longest line of Eternity: O the hight of this Mercy! O the length, the breadth & deepth of Love! Who is able to comprehend it! to know the Love of Christ that passeth knowledge.

Thus for ten years & more, I was led as in a Land of Love, being much accompanied with joy & peace; and often in Meditation, as I was carried forth to various subjects, sometimes of the Love of God, sometimes of the vanity of the Creature: other times I meditated of the unsuitableness of all things in this world wch can nowise be satisfying to an Heavenly desyring soul: But my most usual meditations & admirations were of the Love, mercy & pity of God to faln Man; so yt I was as one that could see nothing but Love, and in all could desire nothing but to be swallowed up in Him, & to be taken to Him; wch earnest desyre was hard to be subdued, and to be contented to † wait my appointed time till my change come. † Many great & eminent answers of Prayer were given, scarce anything I ever askt in prayer, but was answered: he never gave me a desire to ask, but He allwise had a Hand to give and I did often know when I should not ask, by being straitned & could not, so yt by freedom to prayer, or restraint not to pray I knew his will: and though I found it my duty to ask, yet offer'd up my desire allwise to his will, not daring to have any will, whither for my self or others. As for the Things of the world, I willingly did not take thought for to morrow. Of This much might be written, but I forbear.

At the end of these Ten or eleven years (wch was about the 30th year of my age) having some Difficulties to pass through I still bore up: but sometime after the sorrow prevailed: and not having skill to stand fast in the Christian armour, I was as one taken out of a Land of *Apr. 3rd 1667. peace: I felt it as the same hour, even to a minute,* how I was taken out of the Peace & Rest, and immediatly putt into a wilderness to be tempted: where I was to fight my way through, & with the Three great Enemies of Man, viz. the world, the fflesh, & the Devil. And as soon as by ffaith & prayer one seem'd to be weakned, a second did rise up; and as soon as that temptation seem'd to be overcome, a third arose up: so yt I had no time to go off my watch, and even fainted thrô long waiting. And when I did think, & sometimes hope they were dead, then an unexpected one would awaken
so yt at length when I found a sweet Calm, I knew by experience, it was a Cordial before some storm or Trial in the wilderness, where the world, the flesh, & the Devil maintained a continual war, yet did I never question my former comforts, neither was I all this time without great Teaching, & joy in God; in visions of the night when asleep, and some few in the day; wch allwise taught & declared what I was to pass through.

Thus was I carried on about Ten years more; and near the end of these years I felt some great Thing was to be knowen & enjoyed, but knew not what: and I had an hungring desire to know further of God, and how I might understand aright how to worship Him as He required; and yt I might rightly apprehend the Intercession of Christ for us; how He was our Advocate with the Father, and how I should direct prayer to God through Christ; wch I searched in the Scriptures, but could not understand it as I beleived it might be knowen: I was extreme sensible of my own Ignorance, how little I knew of God, and how ignorant of my self, even as one knowing nothing. And as I had near ten years desyred a redeption from my former state, for though I was much stayed & comforted yet I found there was a greater Interruption in my thoughts than I had had formerly; so I did greatly press for the days of old, saying; O that it were as in the days of old, when the candle of the Lord did shine round about me; when I sat under his shadow with great delight! O when wilt Thou restore unto me the joys and stilness of thy Love!

After this for my support, on June 23d/ 1678, a year of Jubilee was proclaimed, & prophesied to me by an Angel or Spirit in a Dream or vision; and after confirmed by another Angel in such a lyke dream, which was as They had said, and at the same time performed to me, to witt, at the end of six moneths, being December 23d/ 1678. But about a moneth or three weeks before, I was brought to that, as to be fully contented to take up my Cross dayly, if it was His will; being satisfied to wait the Good-pleasure^ not desireing deliverance^ of God as I often before had done. And I was no sooner contented (as I have allwise found yt contented Resignation is the nearest way to deliverance) but in three or four weeks at most, on Decer 23d/ aforementioned, I was taken out of this Bewildred place, and put into such a calm as is not to be expressed: that as the very day, hour & minute of my being set in the wilderness were so plainly felt & perceived, being so different an air; so the taking out of it was as sensible, leaving all storms behind me I was as fel into a sweet still
Heaven, and new senses given me as one not in a Body; so yt I felt my self quite taken out of all disturbances of outward sense and sett in a new air or another climate, and another spirit given me that was accompanied with new understanding; being as one who had putt off an old garment, nay like one uncloathed of this mortal Body, and a new Body brought forth to manifestation; wch caused great joy & admiration much more felt than can be expressed.

And in a few moneths after, there opened a view of the Heavenly Canaan (as followeth) ffor wch and for the many Manifestations of The Eternal Love of The Father, through His Son of Mercifull Love, communicated By his Holy and Blessed Spirit, I offer to God alone all the praise, honour, Glory, power & dominion of things in Heaven, & things on Earth, & things under the Earth, as is most due: To whom be Eternal Praise. Amen!

div1.head: A Transportation or Manifestation made to Me, whither in the Body or out of the Body (as Paul saith) I cannot tell; but I was often made sensible; where my Body lay, and that my Eyes did abide open, by my spirit's return to it. which was on Mundays night March 17th 1679.
div1.p: Being in Contemplation of Mount Zion, and earnestly longing to be in Mount Zion state, and also to understand what that extreme Agony meant, wch I had been in fourteen days before, that held me about half an hour when I was in bed. It was like a Dark fflood cast forth from the Dragon, wch was ready to swallow me up; but my alone Defence was Prayer, crying without ceasing, & saying nothing else for the greatness of my Anguish & fear, but O Jesus! O Jesus, hide me in thy wounds! Thus for the space of half an hour, till there became a most blessed & gracious Calm!

And being very sensible of the difficulty of overcoming The Beast & Great Dragon, and to gett out of the Babylonish Principle in our progress towards Heaven, my longing grew still stronger to be in Mount-Zion. And as I was in these desires I thought, but what if God should come & appear to me at this instant? upon wch The fflesh seem'd to retreat, & recall her earnest suit, as framing to my self that the sight of God was terrible. But Faith soon check'd those fleshly ffears, by representing yt This was the Place, wch I did groan, thirst & long for; and yt till I was fitted & made meet for this Inheritance of The Saints in Light, I earnestly desired some comfortable Prospects & Visions of that Glory, as Others have had, to encourage me during my wandrings in this Howling Wilderness; This I say, I had often press'd after, manely, to have some Tastes of the Heavenly, till I should arrive at the fruition of it, thereby to stay my holy impatience: yet at the same time I was afraid lest the sight of such a Glory should make it more difficult for me, to be content to stay here in the Body; and should encrease my thirst, even to fainting for The Living God. These thoughts made me pour our my request crying out, O stay me with flagons, & comfort me wth Apples, for I am sick with Love! † And soon after, it being then near †half an hour past eleven at night, as I lay looking up by the Spiritual Eye of ffaith, I saw Paradise with the Tree of Life
in the midst of it, very pleasant & not to be compared to any thing here below: the ffruits that grew upon it were of the most beautifull & plesant Colours; the leaves were of a most fresh & lively green; the grass under it was young & tender, & of a pleasant green Tincture; I could see no weeds, and all appeared as it had been newly watered.

Yet did not This fully satisfie me; except I might also see the Kingdom of Christ; Then was I caught up higher, where I saw Jesus in the appearance of a Man, all surrounded wth a most glorious Light, wch greatly transported me; for now I knew I was come to the place wch I had so long desired to behold. Whilst I was here I appeared to my self (I mean my Angel appear'd to me, but I understood it not) at wch being surprized, and the fflesh shrinking at the greatness of the Glory, I perfectly felt a Touch on the top of my head, wch drew my spirit out of me, as you would draw a knife or sword out of a sheath, & it cut as it was drawn forth, I felt it cut like a two-edged sword. Thereafter I appeared as a spark of Light, and according to my desire I sometimes mounted up to see Jesus; and then descended again to Paradise; all wch motions were very swift.

After this I desired to see the Father, and after a little stay in the Kingdom of Christ, I was had up to God the Father. But Oh! Oh! Oh the Glory! the Splendor! the Brightness! the exceeding unexpressible Glory that was there! at the sight of wch I threw my self down before Him, crying continually for above a quarter of an hour; My God! My God! I'm now come to the place to wch Thou hast called me; and wch I so long desired to see. I am now come ot enjoy Thee! Thee! being got above all those difficulties I have been so long wadeing through, to witt; The Kingdom of the Great Dragon & Beast with its Babylonish Principle. I can't express the delight I look to see my self redeem'd from all those burthens, letts & hinderances I had so long† groaned under. † Then I saw the Dragon was of a long shape & of a green colour like a serpent; It had four short legs, the foremost the longest; It was terrible to behold, the very thoughts of it since made me almost to tremble: It appeared as if it had lost its prey and given it over. The Beast appeared like a grey-Lyon, & seem'd very eager & fierce to find what was become of his prey; but I feared him not, being extremely pleased to see my self so safe. But soon after the Beast saw me & fixed his great Eyes upon me,
wth his jaws wide open, as one watching for the Prey, wch was in the sight thô not out of his reach. The Bablyonish Principle lay on the ground in the appearance of toys and triffles of several sorts, & of puppets for Children. They were represented to me as if they had been spued out, and therefore were not to be taken up again.

I desyred also to see Hell, wch I saw at a distance, in ye likeness of a dark smoaking ffurnace; even a thick darkness wch comprehended no light. † Then My God told me (as I sat † in a Cloud of light & in the felt Embraces of God the Father his Divine Love, wch I thought I was to abide in for ever, never to go out) that I was not come up to abide there as yet, but yt I was first to pass the briers & thorny way; Paradise being hedged about wth thorns; and none can enter into it but by passing thrô the Thorns & Stones. Then I lookt down ☞ to Paradise and saw such a thorny & stoney way as I had never seen before; being all stones, and no path-way to be seen, nor any Body walking there; the stones were half as high as my self: sometimes it appeared all stones, sometimes all Thorns, and those the highest that ever I had seen to pass. I endeavoured to go, but could not tell where to tread; I took care yt no long Garment might hinder me. I thought I would enquire of Travelers that went that way to direct me (though I saw none) but presently I was check'd wth [looped ribbon] The more we advance in our way to Heaven, thô the difficulties become greater, yet through Grace & Experience we are strengthned to go faster. a stay; They need a Guide themselves. I ecchoed back again, Lord send thy Spirit Truth to guide me! I look'd very earnestly to see whither I could see any one in the same way wth me; at length I saw one whom I knew, who came forward thô the way was very bad, & up hill; and I saw yt the higher she came the faster she went; thô the way seemed worse & worse[looped ribbon].† But at last the Thorny way seem'd to Hide †away & disappear, and in stead thereoff appeared a pleasant River of Glass, wch compassed Paradise; and Paradise appeared much more beautifull & pleasant than before.

Then I desired to behold Christ again, and to see his Heart, as some had seen, wch I beheld flameing wth Love to the saints. Then I desired to enter into the Heart of Christ, and so I did; entring & coming forth again very swiftly
for several times. After this, I was desirous to enter into whole Christ; and presently I was in the Person of Christ, where I felt & saw my self: I saw my Eye in & through Christ's Eye; and I saw my head, neck & breast in Christ's, as through a Glass; so I was satisfied. Yet I desired also to see & feel, whither my hand was in Christ's hand, and I found it was; and I laid hold on the hand of Christ with my fingers, and it felt to the hand that touched, as if it touched another hand; but to the hand that was touched, as if the right hand took hold of the left; (upon which my Spirit returned to my body, and I was much amazed; for I did not think yt I belonged to my body, or should ever have returned to it again: but soon was I caught out of my body again, more swift than an arrow out of a bow:) yea I saw my whole Man in & thrô the Transparent Body of Christ; wch sight did cause unexpressible joy in me, to see yt Christ was One wth me, and I one in Him; The blessed Union, wch I had long desired clearly to understand.

After I desired to see God the Father sitting on his Throne of Glory wth a Rainbow over his head: This was an unexpressible great Glory & Majesty, streaming forth Beams like a Glorious Sun; thô infinitly transcending That we see here in our Orb: in wch Glory were most beautifull & Lustrous colours, somewhat resembling the Colours & compass of a Rainbow, but far more beautifull; wch I beheld † wth great admiration.† I desired likewise to see Christ in his vesture dipt in Blood: then was I immediatly transported into his Glory, and saw his Majesty cloathed wth a Loose Garment; the outside of wch was of the colour of pure Blood; but the Inside was as Lined wth white; wch while seem'd to spread it self over most of the red. I was taken up sometimes wth the admireing Consideration of Christ's Love, whilst I saw his Love-flameing Heart, from wch some Blood streamed forth, and also several silver Chrystaline streams. Thereafter I saw the Son of God in his vesture of Glory appear at the Right hand of the Father, who appeared as before, on His Throne surrounded wth an unexpressible Brightness & Glory, and The Rainbow encompassing all.

I desired also to see the Holy Spirit, wch I saw in the appearance of pure silver Chrystaline streams on the left hand of the Father. Then again I saw the Three, Father, Son & Spirit united into one great Glory, making one great Glorious Light: and I went into Them wth The Elders, and we were all one great Light: Then again They appeared Three
as before; and the Elders apart, and I apart: and I beheld Their Glory. And again I was swallowed up, like a smaller Light of a greater; and changed into the same Glory several times. But none can expect expressions from me answerable to those wonders & Glory, wch there I beheld; they being indeed beyond all expression.

Still continuing to behold this Glory I saw no Angels, and therfore desired to see Them; and immediatly there were several of them compassing part of the Throne: They were like unto transparent Gold, wth faces like Men, having two large golden wings coming forth of each five of their faces, wch was most glorious. † After this, seeing The Streams come † forth from the Heart of Christ, as I had seen before, like to a Transparent silver, I asked, what it was? He said, it was the ffire wch was to purifie the saints. Then I had a mind to see the wounds of Christ, and I looked on his Hands, and the wounds there did glister like the purest part of the Light, wch I saw in God the Father, comparing them together. Thus I abode in this Glory, and would often go into the purest part of the Light of God the Father, and be one wth the ffather; and then come out again, & return as often as I would.

I desired to have an Ancient Christian of my acquaintance there, (who I knew had for a long time desired to see this Glory) that He might come & enter into this Light, from whence God is called the Father of Lights; and a little after He came. Then I desired yt one of my Children might come up, & she came a little after: and then another of them; and so till all were come in: They came in the same order as I had desired it. ffirst of all my ffriend entred into the Pure Light; then all my Children, one after another: and as they came up, I remembred Two little Children, wch died one at fourteen weeks, the other at fourteen days end; and imediatly as soon as I began to desire it, They came like two Bright Sparks, one after another, and entred into this great Light and became one with it; as a Spark is swallowed up of the flame; then They came forth again, to witt, my ffriend & Children, wch were then living, in the same order as They went in; they first wch went in first; all severally, yet all as one case of bodies, I seeing Them all/together, and yet severally through each other.

Then I desired to see all the saints come up to this Glory, and saw Them come like a Glorious White Cloud, two & two together, thick & close, a little behind the right hand of Christ: They penetrated ^ through his heart, came forth again, and entred into ^ into Christ's Body, and the midst of the Glory of the ffather, as we had done before: and
so there passed an innumerable Company, and they still ascended without ceasing, till I ceased to behold, and then They came out of the Father again in the same order as They entred in; they first wch went in first; all severally, yet coming all out thrô each other; wch was wonderfull. All of them sat down round the Throne, wch was then of a very vast largeness; The Elders & Saints sitting roung it: I looked to see whither the Saints had Corowns like the Elders, and I saw They had; though I saw they had none, till They had gone thrô Christ into the Father, and were come forth again, and satt down about the Throne. Their Crowns, as I thought were all of a size, they sitting in great order: the Bottom of the Throne was like one smooth glass. There were many more Angels than I had seen before, all like the former compassing the Throne; on the backside, as 'twere of the Saints & Elders, a little above their Crowns; where They might be fully seen.

Reb. 5. 6. Then I thought what the Lamb was, wch S. John speaks of, saying, there stood a Lamb as -- It had been slain: and I looked, and by the midst of the Throne, near the left side, at the foot of the Father there stood a Lamb, wth its right side towards me, having a bloody place in its neck; and some blood was upon the wool as if blood had run down from the wound: It was alive. Then I desired to hear the Saints sing, All honour & praise to Him that sitts on the Throne. Hallelu-jah! But fearing lest I should not be able to behold so glorious a Melody, I fainted, yet hearkned, and when I could not hear Them sing, my Spirit sand praises to Him that sat on the Throne; but I cannot remember what I sung. I still beheld ye Glory untill it began to descend nearer, and the nearer It came, the less was the Light & Splendour: I said, The Glory is the less the nearer the Earth it comes, or is it not because my Eye of ffaith is somewhat dimmed? Then pressed I with a streaching forward, that ffaith might not fail, but yt I † might see the Glory as bright as I had seen it: † Then the Throne disappeared and was gone; and I saw the Glory of the Father of Lights, far exceeding any I had seen before like to transparent Gold mingled wth a ffirey Light, wch shined down to the Kingdom of the Son. This Glorious Light shined in great beauty thrô the Kingdom of the Son into Paradise below it, as a Reflexion of the first pure Light, and it became more beautifull by far than before shading an unexpressible beauty over all the Trees and flowers, wch appeared all transparent. After this, there was a Sheet of Light drawn before
this surpassing Glorious & beautifull Light; and another Little Sheet seem'd to descent from it like a Cloud of Light upon the Thorny ground, and lay upon it; I saw it as long as I lookt after it, it being near two in the morning when this cast appeared; the whole having lasted about two hours. But the Idea (or representation) of all remained fresh with me, from ye first to the last of it, for some days together yr after.
One thing is observable, yt nothing of all I desired was denied me, but the hearing of the Saints sing, wch I desired wth some fear, otherwise than I had done all the rest.

There was towards the end of This vision as I came nearer the Earth, a Request put up by me (finding I had nothing denied me) Lord, what wilt Thou doe wth This Nation? and Straight way there appeared an Hand & arm stretched out towards Them, with a slight moving of the Hand twice, looking like the waving or putting by of my Request, wth these words; Concern not your self with That: Implying yt I was to attend to my Inward Teachings, and not to look out after National Concerns, or the publick affairs of the world: it being said, saluteing nothing by the way. But Oh! The ravishing & unexpressible joys I felt, when I sat in the delightfull Embraces of the Divine Love! a joy, which as it could never be apprehended by me before, so neither can it in the least be express'd by me now. And 'tis very observable, when God told me I must go down again, because I was not as yet come up there to abide; and when I saw the Beast & Dragon ready to receive me, I was not in the least displeased, neither found I any desire to the contrary, nor any fear; but found my self wrapt up in a quiet stilness, acquiescing in the will of God; with a great Delight in the present Enjoyment, finding my self above the reach of evils for the present.
Severall things are here set down short of what they might have been expressed; but all infinitly beyond any thing that ^ was can be anywise declared of them.

div1.head: June 11.
div1.p: Soon after I was a bed being perfectly The vision of a Beautifull Rock by a Still River. Wth a Glorious Sun ariseing on it. awaked, I saw by the Spiritual Eye, a very pleasant still River, and a Bridge went cross it, riseing in the middle like ane Arch, but narrow; I went to goe upon stone steps (which were there) to goe on the Bridge to a Rock I saw on the other side; but when I came near to climbe, The Bridge went higher like a Cloud or Rainbow; so that I saw, it could not be walked on by a weighty body of flesh, but ane Aërial Body; for the Bridge was a Cloud of air: then I contented my self to look on the further side of the River to the Rock, and I saw most pleasant Greens, wch grew as 'twere out of the Rock; The Rock was exceeding high & large, it appeared like several Greens, and after of other pleasant colours, extream pleasant & beautifull in great variety & beauty: it seemed still like a Rock but a Roack of wonder, the more I wondred at the beauty, abundantly more beautifull it appeared; yet no great Light, but shaded. † On †the right side of This Rock ^ began to arise, but it was so exceeding^ a Glorious Sun glorious that I trembled, and could not behold it, then it went down; after, it arose a little again, but I could not bear it, so it disappeared, though I had a desyre to have born it, and looked for it; and if I did but look towards it, it began to appear; as if it did declare that nothing hindred its ariseing, but my weakness yt could not bear it; and thereby shews his tenderness to compassionate our weakness being in bodys of thick clay.

div1.head: June 12th.
div1.p: Many fruitfull Trees grow out of the Rock. It appears variously.Being desireous to have this pleasant object continued, and further to understand this Rock of wonder, the Idea of rock remained; I saw growing forth of this Rock innumerable fruitfull Trees, cloathed as 'twere wth very large leaves, & large pleasant fruit like Citrons, but mixed with red; the beauty being very pleasant & lovely; as also ^ how it was placed ^ considering by so pure, still & shady a River, and how various This Rock had presented it self the night before, still desired to see fully† And again like a Hilly Country wth a Brook running betwixt two hils, where I saw ye first pure River: and by this Brook appeared a Rock but not so pleasant as That before. it being as 'twere in a shady place; not to be perfectly perceived. After, this vast high Rock had other Trees thick & close of small leaves, and so curious, as if it had been pure Gum-work overspreading it from the top to the bottom, like the side of ane High Hill or Mountain. After there appeared like Clouds a Sea wth waves; then a Still River: †

div1.head: June 18 & 19th.
div1.p: I saw Many small flowers, some white & some blue, and of other pleasant colours grew up on the Rock, as I looked on them, Many fflowers grow out of the Rock in great variety. and gone again, and immediatly others in their room, scarcely to be discerned what flowers they were, by comeing up so quick; and as one disappeared, others came; & so continually ^^ in great variety.of ffl; and a swift passing away of the Hills & Heavens, but the Rock stood still.

It appears transparent, wth flowers of red & white only; and why?The next day, there was a thick Body of Darkness or Plate of black before a Bright Light, wch shined under the darkness and lighted the Rock; do the Rock looked transparent with flowers of red & white, no other colour; I asked, why red & white only, and no other colour amongst so many flowers? It was answered, to shew the Purity of the Saints when washed in the blood of the Lamb.

div1.head: June 21. 22.
div1.p: Its Brightness makes all round it appear like a beautifull Landskip. The thick Body of darkness, (wch the day before had still remained before the Light) came over me, and I was gott beyond the darkness, between the darkness & the Light, which I had much desired; and there was so pure a skie of all colours, as if the Rock had stread its transparent beauty over the Heavens & Earth; so that there appeared a most beautifull Landskip every where, and as in a Glove. Then appeared the Rock, having full sight of it, by reason ^ be towards of a pure light, but yet the back seemed to ^ me: I said, why must I be at the back of it, and not come before to see the Treasuries Its Treasures of Pearle. of Pearle? then it turned to me, where there was such measure of pearle as cannot be expressed, over the whole side of the Rock, going out of it. And I saw my self (my Spirit or Angel) goe Her Angel appears like one pure Pearle. from me, as a pure body of Oriental Pearle, like all one pure Oriental pearle, it seemed such a shineing Beauty; but ye ^ (my Angel) back of it^ was only towards me. The Idea of this Beauty doth ^ me, greatly rejoyce^, that our vile Bodies shall be made like his Glorious Body.

It is adorned wth flowers of Pearle & Rich Stones. Next day I saw the Rock so gloriously adorned wth goodly Pearls & precious Stones, as it was wonderfull to behold; so that I might glutt my sight with seeing: yet after that appeared some thing most rare for curiosity; it was fflowers of pearle, & Rich stones, wch grew in the shape of flowers, with the leaves of pearle in curious shapes.

div1.head: June 23.
div1.p:
As I lay awake (for so all hath appeared, although the ^ or Representations of the whole Idea^ remaines the day after) . This Rock still appeared in its full lustre & great riches, being loaded with many larger Rich Stones, and the Light appeared very splendid before it in flameing streames, wch greatly delighted me. This Light continued, but the Rock disappeared for some tyme; and there Ane Altar with a fflameing Heart. appeared Ane Altar with a flaming Heart upon it, till it became a large fflame as big as the Altar: and at some distance from the Ane Arbour of transparent Flowers. Altar, appeared a most Beautifull Arbour of all pleasant flowers, transparent & of a great length, scarce to be seen at the farthest end; the Bottom as of glass; I looked into it and went in, seeing through the fflowers the Light that lighted it, not as between; but as thrô variety of coloured pure Glass of Transparent flowers: I would have been made Transparent & Swallowed up in them, the beauty was so great; as I have done some other times, when greatly delighted with the Rock, I would have been taken into it, and would sometimes goe & sitt in the hollow of the Rock, under -- Its shadow to content me, seeing I could not be taken into it. The Altar I saw flame several tymes as often as I lookt towards it.
Then I looked for the Rock, and it appeared again: and the Arbour appeared various in its fflowers to what it had before, being larger & fewer greens, more whitish with great beauty: and the skies appeared like a beautifull Landship. I was held in this about an hour at least. The first sight of the Rock was in a shady place, but it ascended still higher & higher, so as Beauty did more fully appear, far above any before.

div1.head: June 25.
div1.p: The Rock is taken into The Pure Light & becomes one with It. After appears as one Oriental Pearle. Still desyreing further to behold the gloruous wonder of the Rock for if we shall seek, we shall find; it appeared with greater glory all over Pearle, and a pure pleasant Light lighted it, & came over the Rock and took it into the Light; so the Rock was become one with the light; then the Light gave back to one side, to shew me that the Rock was in the light; and the Rock appeared like ane Oriental Pearle; and then I understood the Light and the Rock was all one Glory, even the God of Glory. O great was the delight to have such a clear sight of that Rock, wch is Light & Love! O the beauty of holiness! I would have been taken in to it. What shall I say of it? it is beyond expression, no tongue can utter it;[as S. Paul said, He heard things not fit to be uttered, So]This glorious Glory, we have not tongues fitted to express: I'm lost to go about to declare or sett it forth: if you understand what glory is, then you may give a guess to this ravishing overpowering splendidness; I here cease, and express it best, by saying nothing more than Glory! Glory! ^ silently transported ^ being with the rays of its beauty.

It appears as several Pearles united into one, to shew the Unity of the Saints in God. After, The Rock seemed to be several Pearls united unto the one Rock, all as of one Pearle. Then I asked, how This Rock of glory being before but one pure Pearle, appeared like many united into one? It was told me, The Lord was that great Pearle of price, that as his Pearles were many, and yet united into one great Pearle, it shewed ^ the Unity of the Saints, when they come to that ^ such is great pearle of price, and awere made one wth Him; They're made one, by being united in the Rock, like^ growing out of the one Pearle, ^ the Several pearles severally every one founded, & made one with the Rock, though severall pearles.

The reason of the Rocks appearing so variously at first. Then I asked, why the Rock had appeared so various before it came to that Beauty of Glory, it seeming to be as a gross thick Body at first appearance thô beautified upon it? It was said, it is to declare the drossiness thatwhich is in the Saints, and how They grow into this Glory by degrees; and when come to this fullness of Glory, all dross iwas done away, They awere so clarified that they become a† like transparent with the Rock. † The purifying Light must enter the soul ere it can enter into the Light. Then I desyred to enter into this Glorious Light, it being like a glory of Light, but I was told; This Light must first enter into me, to purifie and burn up all the dross, yt I may be purified to enter into this pure Light; then I desyred with panting and hungred & thirsted, reaching forth my whole affections wth strong desyres; and as I panted, it came with ^^ a great overshadowing, penetrating, nay filling; and as I breathed forth my [looped ribbon] This was a feeding on Christ's flesh, & a drinking of his Blood. earnest suit, it still breathed in sweet fresh gales of the Spirit, penetrating me throughout.[looped ribbon] Then I desyred The Saints might feel the same I did, and breathing out desires, I felt as if virtue went out to a ffriend (then sick and brought to my Spirit^) and I emptied, but hasted^ who yrupon recovered to the ffountain, where was enough to fill me and others; for I had
only what I had received, and wanted it breathed forth to others; but this can be as little expressed, as before I said of the Rock: but it was a sweet Life, Love, power & virtue overpowering and filling me with joy, delight & praise; and such one intimate ffamiliarity as if I might have, & do what I pleased, conversing with God as with ones intimate ffriend; nay more, as with ones self.

div1.head: June 26th
div1.p: Meditations touching the Rock, & Its different appearances. Upon The Rocks being so long represented to me and so various, my Meditations were such as these. First its being a Rock did declare it was a foundation that cannot be shaken.
Secondly, It being placed in a shady place, & by a River; shewed that refreshing shelter wch is in The Lord Jesus in the time of Scorching Temptation.

Thirdly, The fulness of delight, that arose from the severall pleasant Greens, the Trees loaded wth fruit, and also from the great variety of fflowers, may be alluded to that of the Spouse Cant. 2. 3.in the Canticles; I satt under his Shadow wth great delight, and his fruit was pleasant to my tast.
Fourthly, a Rock denotes security; for sometymes it appeared hollow, where I might (& did) sitt, and be hid and safe, in the tymes of great danger.
Fifthly, a Rock is unmoveable, so That moved not thô the Heavens and the Earth passed swiftly away.

Sixthly, The Rock did usually stand with one side towards me, and sometyme, the back, to declare: we cannot see but in part, and understand but in part, till glorified; then shall we see him as He is.

† being made partaker of his Divine NatureSeventhly & lastly, The great Treasures of Pearle on the Rock shewed the Riches & treasures in God, and yt He is not only so in Himself, but communicated of Himself to us: was declared * my Spirit or Angelin my seeing *my self go from me as a pure Body of one oriental pearle†, as of the Nature of the Rock; I having many pearles also growing out of this Body of one pearle, as ye Rock had.

div1.head: July 1st
div1.p: a wall of Gold. See p. 25 & 26.For Several dayes before I saw a wall of Gold very high, not to be climbed by sense; I lookt upon it as the wall of The New Jerusalem:^ I was raised to look over it, and saw a pure Body of bright^ It was very glorious. shineing Gold. After, this golden wall seemed to compass three Courts; the first was the largest, the second lesser, the third was like A Building representing The Temple of the Lord.a Court covered & filled with the Glory of the Lord, like a Glorious exceeding beautifull Light.

After appeared a stone Building curiously cutt, wch presented it ^ I said, is This the Temple of ye Lord?self often.^ It went leasurely down at one end to some part of the Globe as is against our foot; I said, what, is it gone to East-India? I often thought on this Building desiring to understand it, but could * See this explained pag. 23.not*. Then there was a most glorious beautifull Light displaying it self variously with great delight for some considerable time together. After yt was a High Hill of ffir-Trees all young ones abouta foot high; then appeared in place of The ffir-trees, Cypress Trees very thick lyke a Grove, wth an Entrance; yet I could not see into it, It was so thick & shady.

div1.head: July 2d & 3d.
div1.p:
An High Hill wth Trees, and a Light yet not lightng Them.This Great Hill seemed larger and had other Trees far more beautifull, and over it a great Light; yet it did not light ye Trees
though it seemed to touch them; out wch I wondred, but had this apprehension of it, that it was Light in it self although itDarkness may be near the Light, & yet comprehend it not. lighted not them; darkness may be near the Light yet comprehend it not; This Light went & lay on the Trees lyke a sheet of light or white Cloud: above this white Cloud beyond it, yt was a very Large beautifull plain, the Trees beneath it remaining and the white Cloud upon them; This plain seemed very smooth & pleasant, and at a distance a* Green field with Flints; and anotherSee this expl. pag. 36. Aug. 9. ffield with Living Creatures called Goats, & like Goats, but declared to be Men. after appeared a Redish Light that made the plain all light. I desyred to draw near the Light to see it fully; ffor as S. Paul said, we shall see Him as He is, & be like him. Such a Translating Sight was this, that I was taken up into it, and saw my self walking to & fro like a Body of light as of the same redish light, wth great satisfaction & delight.

These sweet sights & visions declare God is coming to us,These visions declare, God is a coming if we press after Him. and is in spirit with us; by giving such delights to The Eye of the spirit, if we press after it; This strengthned me to beg of God to give me the spirit of Prayer, and(as Christ when on Earth said to the Deaf & dumb, be opened) to take my tongue & loose it, and open my blind eyes: and there was ane immediate answer with a great quickning & refreshing & earnest prayer; with assurance, yt as He did then let me feel his power, He would answer me; and soon after going to sleep, I dreamed of much enlargement in prayer, & though some I thought came in, yet I went on, not being in the least discomposed. I wait thy tyme O Lord, it being the best.

After, I saw a very large light coloured Marble Fountain curiouslya Fountain ready to run over. declaring God's readiness to pour out of His Spirit. cut, I watched very strictly to gett some of the water, but none came forth; I looked if any small streams did appear, for sure I said, there is water enough in it; and being very thirsty for some, It was said to me. The fountain indeed is full & just ready to run overr upon all Nations: This did greatly stay me, yt God was very near and ready to come to pour out of His spirit upon all Nations. After there were like veins of a Rock enameled that did roynd about this ffountain, which I took to be full of water but they were close sealed up.

div1.head: July 4.
div1.p: Still I thirsted for the water out of the Fountain, that IShe thirsting for the water is made to drink. might drink of the Living water & be filled with the spirit; and I was had up & did drink, supping it up as a thing ready to flow over. This I took to be an answer to the pressing suit I had the day before for it, and for a pouring forth of the spirit on us & on all saints.

Towards evening, having had some prospect of a return ofShe cCalls her self & all her Concerns on the Care of God. prayer concerning some Relations; I resolved in all concerns to cast my self & mine upon the cCare of God, who can do all things as He wills, saying, let it be so, and it is so: and ever hereafter to my selfe obey those Commands as far as The Lord shall enable me; cCasting our Care upon Him, He
will sustain us, giving to Him as to our Heavenly Father (as indeed He is) telling our griefs, and begging his direction and speaking word.

div1.head: July 5th & 6th.
div1.p: The Fountains not running over is because we are not fitt to receive.Being very desyrous to see this Fountain poured forth, I considered it was told me; The ffountain was ready: I saw yrfore yt the delay is because we are not fitt to receive it. Which called me to mind the arising of that glorious Sun at the beginningvid. pag. 17. of the Rocks appearing; and thatwch nothing hindred its arising in its full strength & lustre, but my not being able to bear the exceeding brightness of it; being an unexpressible glory, a pierceing, burning, firey flame as could not be born.

Earnest Prayer for Its pouring forth, & yt we may be fittedStill pressing for this Fountain to be poured forth upon all Nations, yt all may behold His glory; and in particular, yt I might have such a measure of it, as I might declare his Immediate Teaching by some excellency in Life: Soon after, I saw this Fountain so full as the water swelled up even above the top. I cryed; O break forth for this glory, fill our thirsty souls; why^ there's withholdest Thou, seeing^ enough in thy self? nay as if [looped ribbon] desiredst[looped ribbon] Thou to be eased, even like breasts full of milk to be emptied. Where is the delay then? O Lord, it is in us, make us meet, fitted vessels for this New Wine of The Spirit; yt it may not be putt into old vessels: O Lord make us new throughout: O Come Lord Jesus, come quickly! fill, fill us; even so, Come Lord Jesus! Lord are not these thy own breathings in us? yea Lord, I know the Spirit groans in me with strong cries as cannot be uttered.

† There upon was wrought in me a firm belief, that God would sweetlyThe Fountain begins to run over, wch confirms the Belief of God's pouring forth of His Spirit. breath his spirit amonst us at that tyme; I being then to meet with others to seek the Lord, for the more pouring forth of his Holy & blessed spirit, having given us the first fruits, thô in measure, The praise & honour be to Him for any refreshments in this our Pilgrimage. And being th mett, I saw This ffountain appear, beginning to run over lyke a precious oyntment: I was grieved it was so for above our reach that it came not into us; It declared that anointing oyl of the spirit, That Unction from the Holy One yt teacheth us all things. Several tymes was this ffountain thus presented, wch did procure great joy & a firm belief yt He was coming, by the oyntments running a little over on the top of the ffountain, & lying lyke a rich oyntment. And as the spirit did thus declare in me, yt it was coming; so also in a ffriend at the meeting, who knew nothing of that word I had; He also declare yt The Spirit prophesied in Him, He was coming; and was sweetly enlarged, as also afterwards in singing of praise wth great^ And surely The Spirit was wth us thô we knew it not. joyfullness than usually.^

div1.head: July 7th & 8th.
div1.p:
Having sweet breathings & overshawings from the God of all consolation, reviving & making glad the whole inward man: I was muchAn Enquiry anew the use of the ffigure, where the substance is enjoyed. pressing for a clear understanding of my work & duty concerning the receiving the Elements of bread & wine in a sacramental way, having been the day before at that ordinance, and having for some tyme before begged direction, not fully understanding what need there was of the figure*see June 25. p. 19. when we had the substance; for I had fully experienced* what it was the eat Christ's Body & drink his blood, and had it revealed to me in a very high Communion, & overshadowing Incomes, yt this is the Eating Christs body & drinking his blood: I rejoyced in spirit, & said,
now I know what it is; This, this is the eating of Christ's flesh, This is the drinking of his Blood; I feel a vital vivifying, I find Christ is come by his spirit; do this, Christ said, till I come.

I called to mind the Building or Temple curiously cut I sawSee p. 20. about the beginning of this muneth, how it went down & turned over to a Nation against our feet, and I saw a people flock to it in habit like the Indians: That yr might be ane overturn of these outward formsfforms may be of use to call them that are afar off, but we are to wait for the Spirit. as to us, which yet might be of use to call them who had not heard wither there were an Holy Ghost; but as to us, it might depart, and we shall not be left comfortless, but He would send his spirit; for in the place of it appeared The most pleasant delightfull Light, that words are too short to express, and a Fountain full, wch after flower over.

The Incomes of the Spirit are a Sufficient recompense for all Losses.Next day some encouragements I had to hold on our way, what ever we might meet with: if we have lost house or lands for Chr[is]t we shall be Incomes immediatly from Him receive in this Life an hundred fold. O the refreshment in the wayes of God! The sweet delights, the ravishing joy in the souls conversing with divine wisdome, far transcending all painted pleasures compared with this bliss!

div1.head: July 9 & 10th.
div1.p: The delights of the Inward Senses far surmount all those of ye outward wch we are strictly to watch against.Upon serious Meditation I find the great & last to be swallowed up of Life, is the mortal senses to be swallowed up of in mortality: which wisdome does by opening Her divine Treasures & riches, and beauty of Holiness to our Invisible Senses, with various delights, wch far surmounts all outward: such as ear hath not heard, nor eye seen: and^ to our feeling The over powering, over^ by opening shadowing Breathings of the Spirit; & tasting of joyes to come, feeding on Christ.

We had need keep a strict watch against the least motion of ye sensitive Life: Soon after these thoughts we met together to wait on The Lord, to keep that Love-fire warm, wch will put out all Earthly affections, as the sun puts out a fire or darkens a Candle.

I saw when mett together a Pleasant Green ffield for some tyme but did not much observe it; and of a suddeain, lyke a sudden a LightThe gradual arising of a Glorious Sun for some tyme, where I saw the most beautifull shade of blue like heaps of Clouds, & a white amongst Cloud by them; or a Light wch reflected Light with such unexpressible beauty, as sensitive Colours are not to be compared to it, with a Bright Light by it; the Idea^or Representation^ remained very pleasant, and about two hours yrafter seeing it very as at the first, The bright Light by it, as a white Cloud went leasurly over these beautifull heaps of blue; and from whence This Light Cloud came arose a Glorious Sun, as if it had by its ariseing dispersed the white Cloud, and all became clear. I saw the Sun as it arose, till it came to a pretty height; there were some Little fears in me at the first ariseing of This Sun, but when This Sun ariseth in its strength, it will make all Clouds of fearfull Nature to disappear.

and from our faintings will us uprear,
for perfect Love is without fear.

The Sun had a Circle round the edges of pure streams of gold, and many people flocked to it very eagerly to behold it; the Ground was of rough Gold lyke very fine gravel; The People run as if they had^ not understanding as yet what it meant. had a desyre to worship it; so had I, being moved yrunto, but did not^

After, where this gold Earth was, yr appeared a very glorious Light,a Glorious Light being no less than
than a Reflection of The Glory of Gloria.many hundred times larger than the Sun before, and so shined yt the Sun compared to this Light, was but lyke the smallest candle compared with the Sun, for Light & largeness. I said, what is this great Light? it cannot be the Reflection of this Sun that is newly risen, for it so far excells it, yt by its beauty & reflection it darkens it: surely it can be no less than the Reflection of Theat Glory of Glories wch is above: and I saw so Glorious transparent Light hang over it, hovering in the air like a Globe of light; the Reflection of wch was this great Light.

[cross]The next day being in Meditation of That Sun & the beauty of it, and Contemplation of the Brightness of The Fathers Glory, which^ I said was so transparent, beholding it with delight & filled with joy: ^God ^ Glory, Itis all glorious, whither you look on the right hand or on the left; [cross] The foretast puts ye soul in a holy longing for ye possession.& was not able to contain or express ye^but was causing an holy Impatience to have mortality swallowed up of Immortality, that I might not be thus straitned; and how am I straitned thus to be cabin'd up in flesh, and not in the glorious liberty of the sons of God! and as Christ said, so may I truly say; I have a Baptism of the Holy Ghost as with fire to be baptised with, to purge a-way all dross, self & sin; and how am I straitned till it come! O I am even forced to say, Turn away thine eye, for thou hast ravished me! O when shall I be able to contain what Thou wilt give! How Long Lord! holy & true? we can take in but little of Glory here; we can be hold but little of this new wine by reason of our old vessels of flesh; but yet a little while, and He will come, and we shall enter into glory: till then we groan within our selves wth strong cries for the redemption of the Body.

div1.head: July 11.
div1.p: [cross]I saw a Plesant walk of Gravel & Trees in great exactness, and ane Ascent above it more plesant with several walks: After there was a Rich & glorious Building of Agats, large, &l compassed wth edges of Gold, wch joyned the Agats together: It was like a [cross] Rich gates as of ye City of JerusalemGate to some great City, it being high & large. Then I saw another Gate very rich, all of Mother of pearle, & gold, and pillers of some rich twisted Chrystal; I said, surely This is the gate of The City ofNew Jerusalem; This is like a Gate-house, but if This is but like The Porter's lodge, what must The palace be? If This is but the Gate to it, what is The Chamber of Presence?, which is filled with the odours of his glory? Then I saw an open Gallery with Pillers of stone or Marble, & speckled wth Gold, and ona well wth a Bucket of Moyr of Pearle. one side a well near full, with a Bucket of Mother of Pearl chaind with a great Chain to The well.

div1.head: July 12 & 13.
div1.p: The Idea being very refreshing caused me admire The great Riches in God, and conteinn all things besides; making it our business to wait on Wisdome's Teachings for those beautifullA rich Porch discoveries. Beyond the former Gates was another Gate like a Porch with ane Arch over it; there were six Pillers that bore up this Porch, three at a side; The uttermost of a Clear Gold-coloured stone, very beautifull & twisted; The middle Pillers of white smooth stone, lyke an unpolished Diamond; The Cover was of divers large, flat, rich stones of several colours; The ffrong of ye Porch above, and the sides of it, were many beautifull flowers of these rich stones to great admiration; The Gate within was shut, It was of a dark redish Colour, I diligently watched to see it open to goe

in; after some time it leasurely opened, and at the farthest side of the Porch there was such another Gate shut: but finding The first opned not till some considerable time, and at first a little, & so by degrees; it made me think I should not see this open, and then considered that I desyred to have it open to go in; but alas! I must not stay there; O Lord to goe in, & there abide! Lord, when shall it once be? when come to a state of Fixation, and no more go back again to ye ruines, the ruinous places of This world! ffinding my self greatly burthen'd at this state of absense, yea in a holy impatience. Bbut towards night the next day, I became as one still, & said; I bless Thee that Thou dost declare Thy beauty & excellency as refreshing Cordials in this Wilderness, being even wine of consolation: But O when to the State of possession of Father, Son & Spirit!

The soul is comforted in its present foretast & view of Its Inheritance.At night after I was a bed (as for the most part then are the sweetest Incomes) I prayed & obtain'd a sweet acquiescence in God. I considered the great mercy I enjoyed by These openings & visions of Glory, and yrfor ought to bless God: O that hereby we may be in heavenly enjoyments before our tyme! I mean, by viewing our Inheritance before our possession; that although we have not yet ye purchas'd possession, yet may greatly rejoyce to see what we are redeemed to. Surely joy & sorrow are very consistent with our present state, to rejoyce in hope: but O our Ggroanings may well be born with, and doubtless are pleasing to The ffather of all consolation; and He that hears our Ggroans, will come to help & stay our longings, yea even faintings under our burthens of flesh. O we know not how any longer to debase our selves: help us to that Birth of power under our stong Cries for deliverance, yt Thy Kingdome may come, Thy will may be done in us, as it is in Heaven.

After this, I found a sweet still Quietness, to rejoyce in the present visions & declarations of Glory; his will being our great Glory: for then we are glorified, when we can stand still in his glory will.

Then I saw the Inward Gate that was shut opened wide, and it was filled with a white Cloud of Smoak; as with ye Glory of God. After this Cloud was clear'd away, there went from this rich Gate a Long Entrance in shape lyke ane Arbour, very rich with all variety of colouredAn Arbour of rich stones in variety of colour'd fflowers. Rich Stones, in flowers all transparent, and so long asyt I could not see the end of it, thô I went into it: after, it appeared various with great Treasure & beauty, like indeed to a passage belonging to such rich gates and such a Porch as was before.

At the farthest end of This Entrance or Arbour, I saw great heaps of gold pebles pour'd down, wch as I narrowly observed, were all laid for the Pavement of the said Arbour, for surmounting all the riches of this World.

div1.head: July 15th
div1.p: The well & Bucket explained.The well I had seen (the 11th) was much upon my mind, being full of water, & having a Bucket of Mother of pearle chain'd to it. This rich Bucket sure is Faith chain'd by Love to ye well, so as we may goe and draw water of life & strength, virtue & power out of the well of Salvation: O strong bands of Love that hold us! I mean God's love, who loved us first; causeth us to love Him. After this, I saw Rich, beautifull stones like a Wwall, beginning to appear. Aafter -- a Stone cut like aAlso the Wall Coat of maile; it was not to be pierced between, but all of one stone, & beyond it lyke a Beautifull Arbour: This Stone arose to an exceeding height, even to the height of a Mountain; wch did greatly rejoyce & strengthen me, shewing the security & safety that is in God: He is a strong hold, a sure refuge from storms; and They still find it who putt their whole strength & trust under ye shadow of his wing of power.

div1.head: July 16.
div1.p: Considering again of This Wall & also of The Well: O the strong Chain of God's love wch holds the bucket of Faith to ye well! Gods Love and ours are so linked together! God's love is the Chain of the strong power of God to enable us by ffaith, to fetch strength, life & power out of the well of all Comforts: O the Love of God! we are keept by the mighty power, the chain of Love-power thrô Faith to salvation. The Love of Christ constains to obedience, to do his will, yt we may have the purchase & possession: wch possession is in less than Himself glorified with the Father; He in the Father & we in Him: O that blessed Union! The earnest & fervent Love we have for this union causeth these groanings, yea even faintings for God, for The Living God; O when shall we come & appear before him, to see Him as He is, eye to eye; our vail of flesh changed, & being made like his glorious Body, yt The Love where with God hath loved Christ may be in us & He in us: now Christ in us is the hope of Glory; but then we shall be in Christ in the possession, O never, never to return to feed on vision, but come to fruition!

At night I saw that mighty stone wall, all as of one Stone like a Mountain; it declared to me, God was a strong Refuge; what could peirce this wall? what Cannon could enter into it, or above it? The safety in this Bulwark greatly delighted me: I asked, who were there? Surely they must be eminent Saints, such as Abraham & the Prophets, that were so secured? It was said to me, It is my hideing place for the saints; surely Abraham is there, I thought: and as Abraham offred up his only son, ye son of the blessing, O Lord I offer my self to Thee,☞ Our Isaac, the Compleatment of our work in this body offer'd up. my Isaach, the blessing wch I desire to receive (wch is a Body here to glorify Thee in, an Evangelical body) but thy will be done; it is ye Blessing, the compleating the work of Redemption here: yet I will offer this desyred blessing on the Altar of thy will; and am willing to live or dye; a deluge of destruction being ready, as we think to over take us. I thought I offred my bBlessing (Isaac) laying it on ane Altar to die, to go to this Glory being just by it: and the great wall gave back, and I saw many people in it, such as we are, in bodies of flesh; and I was taken in: there indeed was an hideing place till the storm was past: A place of security, it compassed them round, & over them that they could not be seen: and after a little while it opned again, and the People went out, some to the right hand, & some to the left; a very great company; and athe great wWall did go away by degrees wth them, diffusing it self in a thin Cloud of air not much to be discerned; but went by degrees as they went, to declare God's special presence that followed them, yt where They were, He was; and they went not out till his presence went[four dots in diamond] with them: the Presence of God overshadowing (though invisible as to man) is such a defence, as that Bulwark seemed when at its greatest strength.

div1.head: [cross] See p. 68.July 21.
div1.p:
I Saw --a Beautifull Landskip of ffields, but when near them they werea Door opened within wch was all Sun, or a Globe of all bright Glory. all of pure Gold & rough cast, & there shined such a pure, clear & strong light on this gold, that the very reflection wch lay on the ground looked like a Glorious Sun in its full strength, This Light yt shined so bright came from an opening in the Clouds like a Door or Window, wch place within was all day, like all one Sun; a Globe of all Light, a Globe of all Glory, The globe of the Earth like nothing to it for greatness. The Sun^ to Light wch lighteth our Heavens here looks like a bright spot^ the heavens, they being many times larger; but there the Heavens were all Sun; wch glory could not be beheld, but that it opned but a little. O what glorified persons shall we then be, when made able to behold pure Deity! O this is
The Eternity of Glory! no comprehending the vastness: This was pure Deity wch we are sparks off; here the Trinity is in Unity, & the Unity in Trinity; here is in this Light Heat, virtue & power; Light in God ye Father, who is the ffather of Light, virtue in his Son, & power in his Spirit; by which we receive vivifying Life, virtue & power, to subdue all our wills to Himself.

div1.head: July 22.
div1.p: I was -- much in Contemplation of God's power, who is able to perfect whatThe Autheur is strengthned by a view of her former experiences, & a new manifestation of her state. He hath begun & will to the day of redemption, with Meditation & consideration how God wrought worked at first on Me, before I was eighteen years of age, and the doubts I lay under for six moneths; and yrafter how I fell sick, and saw all my Sins as one act written before me, and Hell opened to receive me, wch I looked upon as most due; but after, how God came in with free grace & mercy, wth the witness of his Spirit, applying several places of scripture no longer to be disputed against coming with such a comforting power; and how the Heavens were opned, and an Angel ready to receive me, wch is mentioned more at large in The beginning of the Book. I was also considering what ffigure I saw then, and immediatly I saw The Skie open, and a most pleasant beautifull Angel, as if cloathed wth flesh (wch I remembred I had then seen) that stood ready to receive me. This I lookt upon as only a view of what I had seen heretofore about twenty years agoe.

Hereupon I was requesting Holiness throughout, being the finelinnen of The Saints: and had some fears left this state I was in might not continue, yrfore desired to be with God to behold all his wonders & glory; and I saw a Pleasant Ascent very strait, like a skie, where part of it was like the Colours of a Rainbow & a light, and by it I saw an Opening in the Heavens, where was one in figure like a Man-Child, as I did judge, it was most beautifull, much like the former (angel) wch is mentioned, but larger; round his head was like a sun streaming out: ^I was told, that was me; I was come up; ^ He was compassed as in an Oval much of the colour of a Rainbow. and I might be sure I was there, because I could see my self there, and yt this was to declare to me, to assure me; yt as sure as I saw that there, so sure I was there, and was circled in a Circle of Security, free from danger. I thought yt was not me, for I am in my body; it was said, your body, you know, is not the Man; that is but the shell (and I thought I saw my self like a shell) but the man is desyre, will, & affections, that's the whole of Man, and that yow see here; yrfor yew are here, and so circled wth divine power, to keep the whole man up wth the Lord: This did greatly stay me. The Circle was thick though of the colour of a rainbow, The Circle of security is my great support. This called me to mind, yt I had I had no such cause to feat the loss of these enjoyments; for as former experience had caused some fear, so lykewise they gave ground of hope: for after That ffirst sealing day, as I sawSee p. 4. Heaven opned to receive me; This Comfort & joy continued in such a measure that for a dozen of years after & more, for the most part, I lived in the joyes & love of God, wth the sense of his mercy; not being lifted up nor cast down by the world or outward Concerns. And thô since, for about eleven years have been led in the wilderness, yet never to question whether in a state of grace, or a Child of Love, but had strong consolation yt I was a Child of God, evenas well when under ye rod, for these were but ffatherly chastisements.

These & such like were My Meditations, being much raised in praises to God for his comforts, his frequent visits, declaring his Love andin carrying me out of all sensuall delights, and swallowing me up in his divine embraces; even^ lost in his Love: soon after I saw^ to be
ane Invisible hand circle & wynd round, and move wynding higher, and I saw a small Iron Wyer wond round; I said, Lord! yt my affections may be allwise wynding up to Thee. A little after I saw this hand like a shadow wynd up again, but not the other iron thing, but I followed it with the spiritual Eye, and it ascended wynding till it came to a very great height; yet keept I it in my Eye, andflame 1. at the top was a fflame: I said, Ah Lord! continually wynd up all my affections, till they flame in love to Thee. That still wond higher, then 2.another Flame: I said, O Lord! How delightfull are these fflames of Love wch come from Thee, and desire allwise to be offred up to Thee! And it still wond till it came to an exceeding height, and then a Third 3.Flame; and there was The Flaming Eye of Eternity; and this fflame was The Flameing Eye of Eternitytaken into the Flameing Eye as into its Center. I said, Lord, let me still ascend in flames of Love, till I come to center in Thy blessed, eternal flaming Love: This fflame was a Large Circle of extream bright glittering light, in the middle a peirceing Eye that stood fixed upon me, not in the least moving off me; and I fixed my eye with great strength & comfort, yt This Eye of God was allwise over me, and saw the secrets of my heart, who knew my whole desire was towards Him. I desired this might be my support hereafter, yt as God's observing Eye was over us, so also his preserving Eye for our safety, being encircled in his Power.

After, This Eye was half of it shadowed with this Bright Light like a lid, and it declared so much love, sweetness, meekness & tender-compassion in the brightness of his Love, as did raise in me very great delight & joy, yt God's Eye declared what was in God; as his Observation, so his Love & security was allwise with me.

After some continual delight in this pleasant brightness, I saw some small, bright figures by the side of this Circle of bright shineing Glory; they were exceeding bright, like the same brightness that they joyned to, but I knew not what they were, but thought, sure They way be well call'd Angels of Light, for they were bright as all Light. This Eye of the Trinity, The Circle of light, was many hundred times brighter & larger than The Sun in the skie wch we see.

After some considerable time, The Glory of Mount Zion was opned, where I saw the Center of the Eye in ye Heart of the manifested Glory of the ffather in great Majesty, wth a Brightness of Light about his Head, & a Rainbow; and The Glory of the son of God with The Eye centred in his heart to* Zach. 3. 9./4. 10. declare The Trinity, The Son in the Father & the Father in the Son. After this, I saw in a Low Bush as growing on The Earth, *Seven Eyes contractedThe Seven Spirits of God in Nature. together, then I was instructed; yt God was in all things seeing, & observing, & securing. After some time, I turn'd to rest, and one Eye appeared just before me, but not with such a bright Glory as the ffirst, but a thin light circling round it: I observed it for some tyme; and then another large circling Eye opned like the second, and had some glimpse at first of the Second, but not of the First large bright Eye.

This Eye had a very thin Circle about it, and the Eye was very pierceing not in the least looking off me, but looking as it were thrô me: I said, O Lord, Thou canst look me into Nothing, who can stand before thy pure eyes? what am I to come to Thee! a poor naked spirit ready to shrink at thy power? but Lord cloath me wth the garments of My Elder Brother, the Robe of Christ's righteousness. Then the peirceing Eye diffused into the white Circle, so yt it became more thick & whitish; the Circle & the Eye became shadowed wth Love & sweetness like a lid covering it all over wth Love so yt the Eye lookt thrô this lid. This Love that shadowed was declared to me, to be J Christ wch is the Love of the Father declared to us; and then what Love & sweetness! when God's justice is covered wth Love; and he looketh thrô the Lid, wch is J Christ thrô his Love J Christ; Then we can behold
Him, & go to Him. Then I went out of my self in a Beautifull white robe, and after went forward a little, & ascended by degrees, and went up to This Eye; and the Eye opned fully, and as it were reached down to take me up, and I was taken into the back of the Center & middle of the Eye; and after some stay, a Thin misty Body descended where the other ascended, full of gold, bright light specks, as small as specks made wth a pen and came & overshadowed me penetrating throughout: for this I praised God, yt as before I stood a naked spirit, & so could not go up into God, and having desired the Robe of Christ's righteousness, that was his Divine Humanity, that heavenly cloathing, now there was an acceptance, the Spirit sent down to come into me, to make it a Body fitt to carry up the soul: This had a sweet reviveing quickning & refreshing of my naked spirit. And after some time thinking all was over, I turned my self more fully to sleep, being as to my body disturbed, and I saw this Eye lye on the ground (as by the bed side) wth a thick misty Circle about it, and the Eye very full & plain in the midst: Then IThe Lord's Eye upon the Earth to observe & preserve. observed, saying, Is the Lord's Eye upon the Earth to observe & preserve? O The Safety yt is in this Circle! none can come near nor hurt us. After a considerable time, The Eye gathered up into a round Globe and ascended to the other Eye I had seen: and they both went & entred into the Great Circling Eye of Infinite, bright Glorious Eternity.

After some delight in these objects, I saw a shady place, a shadow like an hand circle round, as if it should say; Observe, and I did; and yr was a dark Earth, ye Earth opned, and yr came forth Light. Ah Lord! Thou art Light in darkness, joy in mourning; Thou causest darkness☞ to disappear: and beyond it in the Element was a Black dismal darkness, very black, which shut up all Light; and when at blackest, there broke out a clear strong light wch dispersed and made the darkness fly away like a Cloud; Itwch made my eyes dazle, as if I had been in the Sun; finding my eyes dazle, I prayed yt The Lord would might enlighten my eyes, yt I might farther understand the things concerning my souls wellfare.
